sources.entry: Surmai - Collaborative personal and family travel organizer. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Docker

summary.one_liner: Surmai is a self-hostable, alpha-stage personal and family travel organizer that lets multiple people plan a trip together and keep booking artifacts accessible offline.
summary.what_it_does: Surmai is a Progressive Web App for planning trips, so it can be installed on a phone like a regular app. It is built for collaborative planning, letting several people work on the same trip, such as splitting up bookings like flights and dinner reservations. It is designed to give easy access to confirmation emails, receipts and other trip artifacts during travel, including on low-bandwidth connections, and it advertises offline access. The README says the data is kept private, and the app is self-hosted through Docker. The frontend is a React single-page app built with Mantine, and the backend is PocketBase. Reference data includes airports, cities, airlines and currency conversion, with translations managed through Weblate.
use_cases: organize travel bookings and confirmations in one place
access trip documents offline while traveling
share trip itinerary with travel companions
how_to_run: Install with Docker by following the installation guide in the project documentation
notable: Collaborative trip planning across multiple users
Progressive Web App installable on mobile phones
Built on PocketBase with its Admin UI for extra configuration
Public demo with a cleanup every hour
caveats: README describes the project as very alpha stage and under active development
Demo site data is cleaned up every hour
Installation details are in external documentation rather than the README
keywords: self-hosted alternative to hosted trip planners
